statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. NVIDIA's delayed post-earnings reversal remains material, while persistent one-way NQ structure has not been independently verified.
recommendation: Tail remains in the WATCH band during the residual NVIDIA repricing window; Stress is extreme but can decay as the event impulse ages if price discovery remains two-way.
headline: Residual NVIDIA repricing keeps Tail at WATCH; persistent NQ continuation remains unverified
body: NVIDIA reversed sharply higher during its earnings call after an initial post-release dip. The delayed second leg is a credible index catalyst, but current public evidence does not independently verify persistent one-way NQ structure with shallow or failed retracements. The next scheduled U.S. checkpoint is the 12:30 UTC claims and advance trade/inventory cluster.

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 clock-hours, Tail was low through most of Wednesday despite rising event Stress, then moved to WATCH after NVIDIA's initial post-release weakness reversed into a strong earnings-call second leg. Persistent NQ mean-reversion failure remained unverified.
outlookSummary: Residual NVIDIA repricing is expected to fade overnight if two-way trade returns. A separate conditional risk window develops around Thursday's 12:30 UTC claims and advance trade/inventory data and the U.S. cash open; Friday's Jackson Hole keynote is the next major policy catalyst.

forecast.analysis: NVIDIA's delayed post-call reversal remains the main live catalyst. Independent persistent one-way NQ structure is still unverified, so Tail stays in WATCH while residual repricing is monitored.

The 12:30 UTC data cluster approaches. Stress rises ahead of claims and advance trade/inventory data, while Tail remains conditional on the price path.
Initial claims and advance trade/inventory data arrive at 12:30 UTC. Event Stress is high; WATCH requires only conditional path risk until post-release structure is observed.
Post-data repricing overlaps the approach to the U.S. cash open. Tail stays WATCH conditionally if directional extension persists with weak retracements.
The U.S. cash open is the main path checkpoint. Sustained opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would support WATCH; two-way trade would reduce Tail.
After the opening window, Tail is expected to fall below WATCH if retracements normalize and cross-asset signals remain mixed.
Mid-morning conditions should normalize unless the open develops into repeated extension after failed pullbacks.
Event Stress should continue to decay if the morning range becomes two-way; persistent directional efficiency would invalidate that normalization.
With major scheduled U.S. catalysts past for the day, normal conditions are favored unless a fresh geopolitical or technology catalyst emerges.
Afternoon risk is primarily continuation versus retracement of the U.S. session move; no scheduled Tier-1 release is assigned to this hour.
Late-afternoon structure remains conditional on whether semiconductors and megacaps confirm the broader index path.
Into the U.S. close, closing-flow concentration can raise volatility without implying Tail unless one-way extension persists.
After the cash close, residual positioning and headlines can move futures, but the next major verified policy catalyst is Friday's Jackson Hole keynote.
Early overnight trade is expected to remain normal unless a new catalyst creates broad cross-asset alignment and failed retracements.
Friday policy-event anticipation begins to build, but Tail remains below WATCH absent observed one-way NQ structure ahead of the Jackson Hole keynote.
